8.	Exactly 15 years before Martin Luther faced the Diet of Worms, on April 18, 1506 the cornerstone was laid for X’s Y that would take over 120 years to complete. Martin Luther abhorred the fundraising tactics used to finance the construction of X’s Y, and that is what triggered his 95 theses. A remarkable succession of architects worked on X’s Y: Bramante designed the initial plan, Raphael succeeded him, and Michelangelo — at the age of 71 — redesigned the building's crowning feature. Bernini later added the grand colonnade that embraces the plaza in front. The building stands on the site where, according to tradition, X was buried after his crucifixion in Nero's circus.
